persona_summary: BIO Junior, CS minor, 36 courses, Good standing
question: I've taken 15-112 and I want to register for 15-213 next semester to make progress on my CS minor. Am I eligible?
false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: 15-213 likely requires 15-122 (not just 15-112) as a prerequisite. The student has taken 15-112 but may have skipped 15-122. A shallow system might see '15-112 completed' and approve, not realizing 15-213 requires the intermediate course.
naive_system_response: A naive system checks if the student has any CS course and approves: 'You've taken 15-112, you can register for 15-213.' It doesn't check that 15-213 requires 15-122 specifically, not just 15-112.
correct_response: You cannot register for 15-213 yet. While you have completed 15-112, 15-213 requires 15-122 (Principles of Imperative Computation) as a prerequisite, which you have not taken. You need to take 15-122 first, then 15-213 the following semester. This means your CS minor will take at least 2 more semesters for this chain alone.
why_multi_agent_helps: The Courses Agent specifically checks the full prerequisite list, not just whether any CS course is done. In the multi-agent system, the Courses Agent has a dedicated prompt to check ALL prerequisites, while a single-agent system processing a broad context may do a quick pattern match and miss the intermediate step.
key_facts: P-036 has taken 15-112 but likely not 15-122
known_traps: Checking only if the student has taken ANY CS course rather than the specific prerequisite
Confusing 15-112 with 15-122 — they sound similar but are different courses
Approving registration based on the student's stated intent rather than actual eligibility
advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) exact prerequisites for 15-213, (2) whether P-036 has taken 15-122 from their course history, (3) the full CS minor prereq chain
